title: Hash maps (dict)
syllabusDesc: Key/value lookups with average O(1) inserts, updates, and reads.
inlineSample:
prices = {"apple": 1.25, "banana": 0.85}
prices["pear"] = 1.50
print(prices.get("apple"))
print("pear" in prices)
desc: Hash maps store data by hashing a key to a bucket. Python dicts keep insertion order, handle collisions internally, and deliver fast average-case lookups.
solution:
scores = {"ada": 95, "alan": 88}
scores["grace"] = 99
scores["alan"] = 90  # update

print("alan score:", scores.get("alan"))
print("contains ada?", "ada" in scores)

# iterate in insertion order
for name, score in scores.items():
    print(name, score)
techniques: Create, update, and delete dict entries
Membership tests and safe reads with get
Iterate over keys, values, and items
Choose keys that are hashable and stable
challenges: Count word frequencies from a sentence
Invert a mapping from name->team to team->names
Merge two dicts where the second overrides the first
notes:
Average lookups are O(1); worst-case can degrade if many keys collide.

Keys must be hashable (immutable types like str, int, tuple).
